mof_description: a manganese metal-organic framework with linear Mn3 trinuclear motifs linked by EE-N3; (?-EO-N3)(?-syn,syn-COO)(?-N2,N3-CN4) triple bridges and pcu topology built by organic linker 1-(carboxylatomethyl)-3-(5-tetrazolato)pyridinium
modification_notes: Article states that near-stoichiometric reactant ratios give products without azide (IR). Base 1 uses KL1 0.1 mmol, MnCl2·4H2O 0.2 mmol, NaN3 2.0 mmol (2:20:1). Stoichiometric for 0.1 mmol KL1 is ?0.15 mmol Mn and 0.20 mmol NaN3 (for 3:2:4 in [Mn3(L1)2(N3)4]). We estimate the ‘close-to-stoichiometric’ region with Mn = 0.12/0.15/0.18 mmol and NaN3 = 0.10/0.20/0.30/0.40 mmol (crossed; 12 combos). Other parameters per base. Outcome: products lacked azide; failure for target.
rationale: For Mn–azide–tetrazolate–carboxylate frameworks 1 (L1) and 2 (L2), the paper states crystalline products required a large excess of NaN3; near-stoichiometric reactant ratios gave products without azide (IR). Plans enumerate those near-stoichiometric ratios versus each base recipe.

modification_notes: Article states that near-stoichiometric reactant ratios give products without azide (IR). Base 1 uses KL1 0.1 mmol, MnCl2·4H2O 0.2 mmol, NaN3 2.0 mmol (2:20:1). Stoichiometric for 0.1 mmol KL1 is ?0.15 mmol Mn and 0.20 mmol NaN3 (for 3:2:4 in [Mn3(L1)2(N3)4]). We estimate the ‘close-to-stoichiometric’ region with Mn = 0.12/0.15/0.18 mmol and NaN3 = 0.10/0.20/0.30/0.40 mmol (crossed; 12 combos). Other parameters per base. Outcome: products lacked azide; failure for target.
rationale: For Mn–azide–tetrazolate–carboxylate frameworks 1 (L1) and 2 (L2), the paper states crystalline products required a large excess of NaN3; near-stoichiometric reactant ratios gave products without azide (IR). Plans enumerate those near-stoichiometric ratios versus each base recipe.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Screened metal:ligand ratios; <2:1 gave unassigned phases; low acidity gave tiny PCN-131 crystals; could not obtain pure PCN-1320 despite varying pH/solvents/ratios.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn2(CO2)4 paddle-wheel SBU pillared by 4,4?-bpy built by organic linkers anthracene-9,10-dicarboxylic acid and 4,4?-bipyridyl
modification_notes: Attempts to obtain pure PCN-1320 failed even after varying pH, solvent systems, and reagent ratios (text). Represented as a combined screen anchored to the PCN-1320 base: M:L < 2:1 (values 1.75, 1.5, 1.0; Zn amounts computed from 0.1 mmol H2adc), acidity varied by substituting HBF4 with no acid or acetic acid (weaker), and solvent varied between DMF and DMA. Lists trimmed to 12 enumerations to satisfy the estimated-combination ceiling.
rationale: Negative conditions from Zn/H2adc MOF study: metal:ligand ratios below 2:1 yielded unassigned phases; and pure PCN-1320 could not be isolated despite varying pH, solvent systems, and stoichiometry (mixtures with PCN-1310 persisted).

mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with Fe(OH) 1D chain SBU built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: At 150 °C with FeCl2·4H2O/H2BDC in DMF and 30 eq acetic acid, after 168 h the solid obtained was Fe2O3 (hematite) rather than any MOF (text; SI Fig. S16). Named inorganic byproduct -> failure.
rationale: Negative conditions for Fe–BDC MOFs under DMF solvothermal synthesis, focused on MOF-235(Fe) and MIL-53(Fe) bases. Failures include amorphous/no solid, dissolution, inorganic Fe2O3, poor-quality alternate phases, and mixed phases.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Screened modulator, time, temperature; some conditions gave amorphous/no solid; phase transformations observed.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with Fe(OH) 1D chain SBU built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: At 150 °C without modulator, shorter times (2–48 h) give MOF-235(Fe)/mixed, not MIL-53(Fe). At 120 °C, 72 h gives poor crystallinity; ≥168 h gives MIL-68(Fe) then MIL-53(Fe). Acetic acid prevents MIL-53(Fe); with FeCl2 at 150 °C + AA, dissolution by 48 h and Fe2O3 at 168 h. Fe(NO3)3 at 150 °C, 72 h gives amorphous. Evidence: Fig. 3b; SI Fig. S17, S21–S22; text: “no formation of MIL-53(Fe) when acetic acid is present”.
rationale: Across Fe–terephthalate syntheses (MOF-235(Fe), MIL-53(Fe), [Fe(DMF)(BDC)], [Fe3O(DMF)3(BDC)3][BF4], MIL-88B(Fe), Fe–BDC-Br), failures arise from modulator identity/loading, Fe-source/counterion, and time/temperature. We list explicit amorphous/no-solid and wrong-phase outcomes and boundary-implied non-working settings from the article and SI.

mof_description: a calcium metal-organic framework with I0O2 (2-D overall) built by organic linker meso-tartaric acid hydrate
modification_notes: Table 2 and SI: at 100 °C forms 6; ≥150 °C forms anhydrous 7. These hydrothermal temperatures fail for 5.
rationale: Across Ca/Sr/Ba tartrates (1–18), phase formation is highly temperature- and stereochemistry-dependent. Outside the narrow windows, reactions yield other hydrates or phases (e.g., meso or DL products) or mixtures, not the target. We list these non-working windows and linker swaps based on Tables 2–4 and SI notes.
